sources.entry: Karabiner - Karabiner (KeyRemap4MacBook) is a powerful utility for keyboard customization.

summary.one_liner: Karabiner (formerly KeyRemap4MacBook) is a macOS keyboard customization utility, now obsoleted in favor of Karabiner-Elements on macOS Sierra and later.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Karabiner as a keyboard customization utility for macOS. It lists changing key mappings (for example, mapping Right Option to Enter), adjusting key repeat speed, and restoring lost NumPad keys on laptops via Fn combinations. It also mentions efficiency modes such as Emacs Mode, Vi Mode, and Mouse Keys Mode. Prior to version 9.3.0 it was called KeyRemap4MacBook. The README states that the project is obsoleted on macOS Sierra (10.12) or later and that Karabiner-Elements should be used there. Older releases are referenced for OS X 10.6 to 10.8 (KeyRemap4MacBook 8.4.0) and 10.4 to 10.5 (KeyRemap4MacBook 5.1.0). The README also includes build instructions that use Xcode, Boost, and a make script to produce a DMG.
use_cases: remap keys on a Mac keyboard
restore NumPad keys on a MacBook
enable Emacs or Vi key bindings system-wide
keyboard customization on older OS X versions
how_to_run: Download the source: curl -OLC - (URL not included in the README)
The make script creates Karabiner-VERSION.dmg in the current directory
notable: Supports Emacs Mode, Vi Mode, and Mouse Keys Mode
Restores lost NumPad keys via Fn combinations
Successor Karabiner-Elements was rewritten for macOS Sierra kernel changes
caveats: Obsoleted and not supported on macOS Sierra (10.12) or later; use Karabiner-Elements instead
Build requires OS X 10.11+, Xcode 8+, and Boost installed at /opt/local/include/boost
Build may fail if environment variables or /usr/bin scripts were modified
